tagline.text: A 170-hectare safari and adventure park in the hills of northern Cebu

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱900–2,500 (per person, depending on admission and rides chosen)

children.text: Set in the hills of Carmen in northern Cebu, this safari park and zoo covers roughly 170 hectares. In one day you can take the African Savanna tour with white lions, giraffes and zebras, watch the bird show, and try adventure rides such as the zipline and ATVs.

Cebu Safari and Adventure Park is a large safari park and zoo in the hills around Barangay Corte in the city of Carmen, on the northeastern side of Cebu island. The park covers about 170 hectares, which Wikipedia describes as part of a private estate of roughly 2,000 hectares. It was conceived by Michel J. Lhuillier, chairman of the M. Lhuillier Group, a name known in the Philippine money-transfer business, after he visited the San Diego Zoo, and it opened in February 2018.

About 1,000 animals of more than 100 species live in the park. In the African Savanna area, grazers such as zebras, giraffes, elands, wildebeest and impalas roam wide grasslands and can be seen up close from a tour tram. There are also big cats such as tigers, white tigers, white lions and cheetahs, plus orangutans, crocodiles, and a bird area with parrots, owls and eagles. Native Philippine animals and birds are exhibited as well.

It is not only about animals. There are garden areas such as Michel's Garden and the Gardens of the World, and the bird show is included in your admission ticket. For an extra fee you can also try adventure attractions such as ATVs, ziplines, sky bikes, a giant swing and cave exploration. The park is about 1.5 to 2 hours by car north of Cebu City, which makes it a popular day trip for families who have already seen Cebu's main sights.

Note that the park is far from Cebu City and Mactan, and last admission is early, at 1:30 PM. Some sources say the savanna tour and bird show are closed or reduced on Mondays and Tuesdays, so check the day of the week first when planning.

blocks.title: Aviary dome and Birds of the World

children.text: Inside the large aviaries you can see scarlet macaws, chattering lories, eagles and owls up close. Because the birds may bite shiny objects, you are asked to remove earrings and necklaces before entering.
The park has Bengal tigers, white tigers and cheetahs, and tiger feeding times are posted separately. The park's notice gives about
in the morning for the orange Bengal tiger and about
in the afternoon for the white tiger, but schedules can change.

blocks.title: Michel's Garden and Gardens of the World

children.text: A walking trail with a 40-year-old orchid collection, and gardens landscaped to represent the continents. They are a pleasant place to rest between animal areas during the hot part of the day, with plenty of photo spots. Both are included in admission.
Wikipedia lists a zipline about
1.3km
long at about
above sea level. There are also an ATV trail, sky bikes and a giant swing, all charged separately from admission. Age and weight limits are strictly enforced, and rides stop in heavy rain or wind.

A viewing deck lets you stand at eye level with the giraffes, and a petting area with small animals such as goats and rabbits also operates. If you are traveling with children, check the morning and afternoon opening hours and plan around them.

items.title: Full-day plan
items.subtitle: Leave Cebu City and see the park over a day

children.text: Leave Cebu City or Mactan. Without traffic the drive takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
to
2 hours
. Leave with time to spare so you arrive before last admission at
Arrive, buy your tickets and pick up a map. Take photos near the fountain at the Welcome Pavilion, then board the tram.
Start with the White Lion Safari and the tiger, orangutan and crocodile areas. The animals are more active in the morning.
Visit the aviary dome and the Birds of the World area. Remove your earrings and necklaces first.
Have lunch at Base Camp or The Outpost. Filipino and Western dishes, pizza and pasta are available, and a meal costs about ₱280–500 per person.
Ride the African Savanna tram. Operating hours are short, so check the notice board beforehand.
Watch the bird show. It lasts about 30 minutes and is included in admission.
Walk through Michel's Garden and the Gardens of the World, or try one or two adventure rides such as the ATV or zipline.
Pick up souvenirs and the exit photo service, then head back to Cebu City. It is better to be down the mountain road before dark.
Opening hours and show schedules change with the day of the week and the season. Check the park's official Facebook page or website for the latest notices before you go.

items.title: Adventure-focused plan
items.subtitle: If you want to enjoy the rides

children.text: Enter as soon as the gates open (8 or 9 AM, depending on the source) and go straight to the ATV and zipline counters. Popular rides get long lines in the afternoon, and sign-ups close early.
Ride the ATV trail and zipline first, then the giant swing and sky bike.
After lunch, take a short loop through the bird show and animal areas, then leave.
Sign-up for the ATV and zipline reportedly closes early in the afternoon, well before last admission, so it is safest to arrive in the morning if you want to ride.
There are several flights a day from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), and the flight takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
From the airport to the park is about
2 hours
to
2 hours 30 minutes
by car. Because last admission is early, a morning flight is more convenient.

items.title: By public transport from Cebu City

children.text: Take a Carmen-bound bus from the Cebu North Bus Terminal. The fare is reportedly about
, and you should ask the conductor to drop you at Carmen Plaza.
From Carmen Plaza, go to the park by van (V-Hire) or motorcycle taxi (habal-habal). Many sources give about
per person, and the last
8km
is an uphill mountain road.
Vans from the park back to Carmen Plaza run only in the afternoon. Decide your return time in advance.
Public transport can take about 2.5 to 3 hours one way in total.
From Cebu City, follow the national highway north through Mandaue, Liloan, Compostela and Danao to Carmen. It is about
80km
from the city center.
Near Carmen National High School, turn at the signboard and climb the mountain road for about
8km
to reach the park.
Many sources say you can park inside the park.
You can book a round-trip car with a driver from Cebu City or Mactan on booking platforms such as Klook. Prices vary by season and group size, so check when booking.
Taxis and Grab charge high one-way fares and a ride back is hard to find, so it is better to negotiate a round trip that includes waiting time.
It is best to go in the morning, when the animals are active and the sun is milder. Weekdays have lower admission and shorter lines, while weekends and holidays cost more and are crowded.

November to May is relatively dry in Cebu and suits outdoor plans. On rainy or windy days the zipline and giant swing may stop. Some sources say the savanna tour and bird show do not run on Mondays and Tuesdays, so if possible go from Wednesday to Sunday.

Inside the park you will find Base Camp (Filipino food), The Outpost (Western food), Pizzeria Michelangelo (pizza and pasta) and Michel's Pavilion, which runs a weekend buffet, plus snack kiosks such as Mr. Potato and Auntie Anne's. Outside food and bottled drinks are not allowed and bags are checked, so bring water in a reusable tumbler.

Inside the park you can stay overnight in Safari Cabins, Safari Camp or glamping tents. Check the official information for rates and what is included. There are also places to stay in Carmen town and Danao, about 15 to 30 minutes from the park by car. Staying in Cebu City or Mactan and making a day trip is the most common plan.
Last admission is
. Latecomers cannot enter, so arrive in the morning.
Prices rise often. Check the official Facebook page for the latest notices on admission and rides. Online bookings carry a fee and cost more than buying on site.
The savanna tour and bird show may be closed on Mondays and Tuesdays, so go between Wednesday and Sunday.
Closed shoes and comfortable clothing are required for ATVs and rides, and skirts and loose accessories are not allowed.
Remove earrings and necklaces before entering the aviary, and do not use flash photography.
There is a lot of walking and some slopes, so use the tram and bring a hat, sunscreen and a tumbler of water.
Bring plenty of cash. Some outlets accept cards, but others do not.
The photo that staff take at the exit reportedly costs about
. You do not have to buy it if you do not want it.

Last admission is early and shows and tours are closed on some days, so be sure to check the official information before you visit. A temporary closure was reported right after the late-September 2025 earthquake, but the park is operating again.
The final stretch of about 8 km of mountain road can be slippery in the rain, so drive carefully.
Adventure rides have age, weight and health requirements, and you cannot ride if you do not meet them. Cave exploration requires a minimum age of 7.
Do not feed the animals or shout. Pets are not allowed, except service animals.
If rides stop because of rain or wind, refunds are reportedly difficult and tickets are instead rebooked for another day.
Some reviewers say the cheetah and crocodile enclosures are cramped, so you may want to explain this to children beforehand.
A large city in northern Cebu about
30 minutes
by car south of the park, with boats departing for the Camotes Islands.
A coastal town on the way back to Cebu City, a good place for a rest stop and a meal.
Islands reached by boat from Danao port, with beaches and caves; they pair well with the safari for a two-day, one-night trip.
The central hub and starting point, with city sights and shopping malls.
